title: Degree of topological categoricity of Baire space
formal: Does Baire space have a least Turing degree of topological categoricity?
definitions: A computable metric presentation is a countable dense sequence (p_i) with distances d(p_i,p_j) uniformly computable: on input i,j,k an algorithm returns a rational within 2^(−k) of that distance. Take its metric completion. A name for x is a sequence of indices a(k) such that d(p_a(k),x)≤2^(−k). A map is computable relative to an oracle D if one oracle algorithm transforms every name of x into a name of its image. A computable homeomorphism here is a bijection with both it and its inverse computable in this sense. Metrics need not be preserved. Algorithms may depend on the pair of presentations; no uniform extraction from presentation indices is required. Baire space is N^N with the product topology of discrete N, for example the complete metric d(x,y)=2^(−min{i:x(i)≠y(i)}) for distinct sequences and d(x,x)=0. Let C be the set of Turing degrees d such that every two computable presentations of spaces homeomorphic to N^N have a homeomorphism whose two directions are computable with an oracle of degree d. Turing degrees identify sets that compute each other by oracle Turing machines and are ordered by oracle computability. The target is ∃d∈C ∀e∈C d≤_T e. It asks for a least element, not merely a minimal element or a common upper bound. The choice of reduction and homeomorphism may depend on the presentations.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the stated proposition or its negation, for precisely the specified model. Identification of a candidate degree must include minimality among every sufficient degree; showing that no least element exists also resolves the target.
context: Problem 28 asks whether the least degree exists; it is not a request only for some sufficient oracle.
why: A least degree would measure the computational information required to identify arbitrary effective presentations of a basic space.

import_provenance.original_title: The degree of topological categoricity of Baire space
import_provenance.original_statement: Is there a least Turing degree d such that every two computable presentations of Baire space omega^omega admit a d-computable homeomorphism? If such a degree exists, identify it.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The maps are homeomorphisms rather than isometries; this is the topological categoricity problem stated by Ng, not ordinary categoricity of a discrete structure.

sentences: Baire space consists of all infinite sequences of natural numbers.
Its computable presentations need not have effectively comparable metrics.
A degree is sufficient if it computes suitable homeomorphisms for every pair.
The target asks whether the sufficient degrees have a least member.
Pair-dependent choices are allowed, but minimality must hold in the full Turing order.
